title: Telerik UI for MAUI Documentation Accessibility Audit

Executive Summary.assessment: The documentation has a useful accessibility foundation, but recurring source-authoring patterns reduce nonvisual navigation and comprehension. Prioritize table relationships and text alternatives to instructional media, followed by heading, list, link, and code improvements.
main_risk_areas: Raw HTML environment tables lack header cells, and some Markdown tables leave relationships implicit.
Instructional videos have descriptions but no article-level transcript links or equivalent written lesson paths.
Bold step numbers and inconsistent heading levels weaken semantic navigation.
Some image descriptions name a feature without explaining the comparison or demonstrated result.
A small number of repeated link labels lead to different destinations.
Executive Summary.estimated_content_quality_maturity: Developing: metadata, named links, image alternatives, language-tagged fences, and reusable content are established, but the inspected contributor guidance does not operationalize accessibility review or enforcement. This is a qualitative assessment, not a measured maturity certification.
Executive Summary.critical_assessment: No Critical finding was substantiated. The source review did not establish a widespread barrier that completely prevents understanding; repetition alone does not establish Critical severity.
positive_observations: No empty alt text was found among the 1,309 recognized inline Markdown image references.
No exact generic labels matching here, click here, this article, this link, read more, learn more, or more were found among the recognized inline links.
Of 1,765 recognized fenced blocks, only one opening fence lacked a language tag.
All ten detected video iframes have title attributes.
Reviewed Markdown data tables generally have header and delimiter rows; complexity alone is not a failure.
Executive Summary.scope: Only Markdown source, authoring practices, and referenced documentation assets were assessed. No Telerik MAUI runtime functionality, product keyboard or screen-reader behavior, Report Viewer, Report Designer, generated-report compliance, or accuracy of product accessibility claims was evaluated.
Executive Summary.change_scope: This report records findings and recommendations. It does not remediate articles, modify publishing behavior, or introduce automation.

Methodology and Coverage.skill_application: Apply the skill's eight dimensions to source evidence. Embedded media, contextual image explanations, and repository authoring practices are additional requested checks; do not treat iframe titles as image alt text or silently add media scores to the eight-dimension formula.

severity_definitions.Critical: Verified prevention of understanding or a significant, widespread barrier.
severity_definitions.High: Meaningful loss of access to instructional content or data relationships; remediate soon.
severity_definitions.Medium: Reduced accessibility or usability; address during scheduled content maintenance.

scan_procedure: Enumerate baseline files with git -C /home/runner/work/maui-docs/maui-docs ls-files '*.md'. Exclude .github skill reference articles from content metrics; inspect the accessibility skill separately.
Read UTF-8 with optional BOM; integrations/document-processing-libraries.md required a Windows-1252 decoding fallback. No source encoding was changed.
For the main scan, skip initial YAML front matter and fenced code bodies. Recognize indented or blockquoted backtick and tilde fences; distinguish opening fences from closing fences.

Count ATX headings, forward heading-level jumps, inline Markdown images and links, iframe elements, and pipe-table rows with adjacent empty cells. Inspect duplicate link-label candidates manually, normalizing slug whitespace and excluding template directives.

Supplement with raw-source searches for HTML tables without th elements, bold numeric procedure markers, alternate callout forms, and large fenced examples. These supplemental pattern counts are candidates, not parser-certified violations.

Manually inspect cited line ranges and surrounding sections across controls, installation, onboarding, Knowledge Base, theming, font icons, and contributor guidance. Confirm representative findings rather than treating every regex match as a failure.
Use absolute paths and one-based source lines at the baseline commit. Quotes are exact excerpts within the cited ranges, not claims about rendered HTML.
Score five reviewed articles using the skill's JSON fields and weighted formula. Do not extrapolate their scores to the entire repository.

pattern_counts.interpretation: All 17 reusable templates and all 271 Knowledge Base articles. Templates are fragments; Knowledge Base titles may be generated from metadata. Not counted as 288 confirmed defects.
File count, not count of extra headings. Includes 13 articles requiring outline review; see A05.
Transitions in each file's source outline, not the number of all headings that may need adjustment. Includes unpublished source.
Presence check only; not a claim that every alternative conveys equivalent information.
Limited to the labels listed in the positive observations; not proof that all links are unambiguous.

pattern_counts.pattern: Pipe-table rows with adjacent empty cells
pattern_counts.interpretation: Row candidates, not a count of individual empty cells; determine whether a blank is intentional before remediation.
Raw-source matches, all in Knowledge Base articles; representative confirmed example A02.
Raw-source candidates for semantic-list conversion, not 1,847 separately confirmed failures.
Confirmed in A15. C#, XAML, and other existing language labels were not treated as missing labels.

pattern_counts.pattern: Image alternatives containing overview, example, image, screenshot, or control
pattern_counts.interpretation: Human-review queue only. These words are legitimate in many alternatives; do not replace them automatically.

pattern_counts.pattern: Prose/source matches for above, below, left, right, red, green, or blue
pattern_counts.interpretation: Human-review queue only. Named controls, explicit text labels, color examples, and code identifiers do not by themselves establish sensory-only instructions.

limitations: Repository-wide automated candidate detection is not a manual audit of every article. Detailed findings are representative confirmed groups, not an exhaustive defect inventory.
Regex counts cover recognized syntax, not every CommonMark construct; reference-style links, indented code, escaped syntax, and custom components require parser-aware follow-up.
Unpublished and repository-only sources remain in inventory totals. Do not interpret article_candidates as the number of live documentation pages.
The publisher was not run. Generated H1s, landmarks, callout semantics, table header associations, custom article cards, tabbed-code navigation, and accessibility-tree behavior were not verified.
External snippets referenced by snippet IDs are outside this checkout. Only their surrounding source explanations were assessed, not the injected examples.
Referenced image paths and article context were inspected; not every asset was visually inspected. Exact screenshot colors, embedded image text, GIF timing, and flash behavior were not certified.

YouTube captions, audio descriptions, transcripts hosted off-site, and player interaction were not tested. Missing article-level alternatives must not be reported as proof that the videos lack captions.
No measured Flesch-Kincaid grade or WCAG conformance verdict is asserted. Readability recommendations are based on inspected prose.

Absent constructs receive 5 with an explicit not-applicable rationale in sample scores to preserve the skill's fixed denominator. This can raise scores for short pages and does not establish full accessibility.

This is a verified discoverability gap, not proof that the external lessons are inaccessible.

Detailed Findings.recommended_remediation: Keep a concise comparison table and move long descriptions into named subsections. Explicitly state inherited, not-applicable, or unspecified values after editorial verification. Retain the existing lead-in and header row.

Detailed Findings.recommended_remediation: Name destinations distinctly: DataPager, Radial Gauge, Horizontal Gauge, and GridSplitter. This is a link-label correction, not an evaluation of the documented controls.

Detailed Findings.impact: The same DataPager link text leads to an overview and a styling article. The surrounding list supplies visual context, but an isolated links list loses that distinction.

Detailed Findings.impact: Identical alternatives identify two different illustrations: image-operation toolbar items and an editing dialog. Neither alternative communicates which illustration the reader has reached.
Detailed Findings.recommended_remediation: Describe each screenshot's purpose distinctly and place essential labels or relationships in adjacent text. Verify exact visible details with the asset owner before expanding the description.

evidence.quote: The next image shows the differences and similarities between the Purple and Purple Dark swatches when applied to the AutoComplete control.

Detailed Findings.impact: The article promises a comparison, but the alternative only says 'Telerik .NET MAUI AutoComplete with applied theme' and the adjacent sentence does not state the differences. Nonvisual readers receive the topic without the promised comparison.
Detailed Findings.recommended_remediation: State the relevant similarities and differences in prose after checking the screenshot, and use concise alt text identifying the comparison. Do not infer contrast compliance or invent exact colors.
Detailed Findings.example_correction: Start the alternative with 'Comparison of AutoComplete with Purple and Purple Dark swatches'; add a verified textual comparison rather than relying on that label alone.

Detailed Findings.category: Animated image alternatives and expected outcomes

evidence.quote: ![End result for setting the visual states of the Telerik UI for .NET MAUI Entry control](images/entry-visual-states.gif)

Detailed Findings.impact: The outcome is delegated to a GIF with generic 'End result' text. Readers who cannot perceive the animation must reconstruct the example's intended states from the XAML rather than read a short result explanation.
Detailed Findings.recommended_remediation: Add a static written walkthrough of the states illustrated and what the sample changes in each state. Explain the example's outcome using state names and text, not color alone.
Detailed Findings.example_correction: Summarize the sample in prose: 'The XAML sets FontSize to 35 for Normal and assigns BackgroundColor values for Focused, Disabled, and Unfocused.' Confirm which transitions the GIF actually demonstrates before describing its sequence.
Detailed Findings.limitation: No claim is made about GIF flashing, pause controls, or Telerik Entry runtime accessibility.

evidence.quote: 3. Create a `ViewModel` with sample data and a command for generating the spreadsheet.

Detailed Findings.impact: One 203-line C# body follows a single broad lead-in. It combines sample data, commands, and export methods without a prose map or intermediate navigation, increasing serial-reading effort.
Detailed Findings.recommended_remediation: Keep a complete copyable example, but precede it with a short map of the methods and key customization points. Consider smaller explained sections plus a complete-source link, and state the expected sample outcome in prose.
Detailed Findings.example_correction: Add a 'Read the example' list covering data initialization, command execution, worksheet creation, and ExportData. Do not change or assess spreadsheet output accessibility as part of this documentation fix.

Detailed Findings.impact: The opening fence at line 45 has no language identifier. Language-aware reading and highlighting tools must guess the namespace declaration's language.
Detailed Findings.recommended_remediation: Add the existing repository's XAML language tag to the opening fence; retain the introduction.

evidence.quote: applications for cross-platform implementation targeting Android, iOS, macOS, and Windows from a single shared code-base.

Detailed Findings.impact: The opening sentence combines a marketing claim, purpose, platform list, and code-sharing explanation. Its length exceeds the skill's 25-word target and increases reading effort before readers reach the tasks.
Detailed Findings.recommended_remediation: Split the introduction into short, direct sentences and prefer concrete purpose over stacked promotional qualifiers.
Detailed Findings.example_correction: Telerik UI for .NET MAUI provides controls for mobile and desktop applications. You can target Android, iOS, macOS, and Windows from a shared codebase.

evidence.quote: >Currently, the DataPager does not support the DataGrid `LoadOnDemand` collection.

Detailed Findings.impact: An exceptional compatibility statement uses an untyped blockquote rather than the designated admonition syntax. Its role is less consistent with typed notices and cannot be processed uniformly from source.
Detailed Findings.recommended_remediation: Use a typed note for supplemental constraints and an important or warning type only when the content warrants it. Verify rendered semantics separately rather than assuming a source marker guarantees an ARIA role.
Detailed Findings.example_correction: >note Currently, the DataPager does not support the DataGrid `LoadOnDemand` collection.

Detailed Findings.impact: Each row repeats the product prefix and nearly repeats the adjacent icon name in its alternative. In a long icon catalog, this adds repeated speech without describing additional shape information.

Detailed Findings.impact: ASCII and CRC appear without expansion, and length cells use the unexplained abbreviation 'bzw.'. These interrupt comprehension for unfamiliar readers and readers of the English article.
Detailed Findings.recommended_remediation: Expand American Standard Code for Information Interchange (ASCII) and cyclic redundancy check (CRC) on first relevant use. Replace 'bzw.' with a verified explicit English relationship, not an assumed translation of the data.
Detailed Findings.example_correction: Use 'cyclic redundancy check (CRC)' rather than 'CRC check'; ask the article owner what the paired length values mean before rewriting them.

evidence.quote: please use only standard Markdown syntax, and make to preview your additions or changes before sending us a pull request.

Detailed Findings.impact: The contributor ground rules require a preview but provide no actionable checks for headings, alternatives, table semantics, link labels, media, or code explanations. Repeated defects can pass a visual-only review.
Detailed Findings.recommended_remediation: Add an accessibility checklist and link the existing accessibility skill. Explain publisher-specific constructs and how to review their generated semantics; require source checks plus an appropriate documentation preview.

Immediate (0-30 days): Documentation maintainers: address A01-A03 first, then the remaining Immediate Action Required articles. Record an owner and verification result for each finding group.
Media owners: supply verified transcript or equivalent-written-lesson links for onboarding and confirm caption accuracy separately.
Editors: correct distinguishable link labels, blank table meanings, and confirmed heading skips in small source-only PRs.
Reviewers: use the existing accessibility skill and the checklist proposed in A20 for new or changed articles.
Short Term (1-3 months): Content owners: review the repeated procedure and HTML-table candidates by component or Knowledge Base batch; avoid mass regex rewrites.
Documentation tooling owners: establish changed-file checks for heading structure, fence languages, image alternative presence, and table structure, with a baseline for existing issues.
Content and media owners: audit the remaining embedded-video articles and image-comparison pages for verified textual equivalents.

Publisher owners: verify Knowledge Base title generation, effective heading outlines, custom-card labels, callout announcements, and injected/tabbed examples in a documentation preview. Limit this to the documentation site.
Long Term (3+ months): Documentation owners: maintain a periodically refreshed inventory and track resolved finding groups, remaining candidates, and exception owners.
Documentation reviewers: sample newly published learning paths with assistive technology and narrow-screen or zoomed reading experiences; do not extend this review into product runtime testing.
Media owners: include transcripts, visual explanations, and caption review in the documentation asset lifecycle.
Contributor-experience owners: integrate accessibility rules into templates and PR review, and periodically rescore representative articles using the same weights.

accessibility_guidance: Treat image alternatives as equivalent-purpose descriptions, not an attribute-presence requirement. Provide extended text for comparisons, diagrams, and instructional animation.
Describe actions with named targets and outcomes. Words such as above or below may supplement, but must not replace, an identifiable target.
Do not use color as the sole meaning carrier. Color values in sample code and named theme variants are not automatically violations.
Require verified text alternatives for instructional media and document ownership for caption and transcript updates.
markdown_authoring_standards: Require one effective H1 per published page and no skipped heading levels. Document Knowledge Base title injection and fragment exceptions before adding source H1s.
Use ordered lists for ordered tasks; indent all associated code and snippets under the correct step.
Use descriptive, destination-distinguishable link labels. Keep names consistent for the same target without requiring exact identity for every anchor context.
Use tables only for genuine relationships, with headers and meaningful cells. Explicitly label inherited, empty-string, unavailable, or not-applicable values after confirmation.
Use established typed admonition syntax for notices; reserve severity types for their intended purpose.
Tag every fenced block, introduce it, explain replacement values, and state useful outcomes. Provide a navigation map for lengthy examples.
Expand less-familiar acronyms on first use and aim for concise active sentences, without rewriting legal text or necessary technical identifiers.
documentation_review_processes: Review source heading outline, link list, table linearization, and image-independent comprehension, not just visual layout.
Preview using the actual documentation publisher when changing includes, snippet nesting, callouts, or custom components.
Treat automated matches as candidates until context confirms a violation; include rationale for intentional exceptions.
Do not characterize a source-only audit as a rendered-site WCAG conformance test or product accessibility assessment.
contributor_instructions: Extend the README contribution ground rules with the checks in A20 and link the existing accessibility skill.
Explain front matter, fragment regions, slug links, snippet directives, and tabbed fences so generic Markdown rules do not create false positives.
Ask contributors to describe alternative-text changes, media-equivalence checks, and any publisher-preview limitations in their PR.
Provide good and bad source examples for semantic procedures, tables with explicit values, distinguishable links, and introductory prose for code.

Candidate Inventory.interpretation: Complete file-and-line lists for these five scan patterns at the baseline commit. These are review queues, not additional confirmed finding groups; lines identify the detected transition, second H1, table opening, empty row, or media embed. Publication status and publisher expansion still require review.

Score Interpretation: Scores use the eight skill dimensions and round the weighted mean to one decimal place with half-up rounding. They are illustrative source-article scores, not a repository score or severity formula; for example, the near-perfect video article score does not account for the additional embedded-media finding A03. Minor score observations are not separately counted as Detailed Findings groups.

Validation.approach: Report-only change: validate JSON syntax, finding IDs and severity totals, priority-to-finding mappings, score weights and arithmetic, baseline file paths, line ranges, and exact evidence excerpts. No product build or runtime tests are relevant.
follow_up_acceptance_checks: Revised tables retain all information and support understandable linear reading.
Revised heading outlines preserve one effective page title and sequential levels after publisher expansion.
Converted procedures expose ordered-list structure without separating code or snippets from their steps.
Each instructional image or media item has a verified useful text equivalent; an attribute-presence check alone is insufficient.
Link labels distinguish distinct targets in an isolated links list.
All follow-up work remains limited to documentation accessibility.
